chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar. He said: al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: My father narrated to me, from his father (peace be upon them both):

That al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was the most devout of the people in his time, the most ascetic, and the most virtuous. When he performed Hajj, he would perform it on foot, and sometimes walked barefoot. When he remembered death, he wept; when he remembered the grave, he wept; when he remembered the Resurrection and the Gathering, he wept; when he remembered the passing on the Sirat, he wept; and when he remembered the presentation before Allah the Exalted, he gasped with a gasp that would cause him to faint. When he stood in his prayer, his limbs trembled before his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. When he remembered Paradise and the Fire, he would be agitated like one stung by a snake, and he would ask Allah for Paradise and seek refuge from the Fire. He would not recite 'O you who believe' from the Book of Allah except that he would say: 'I am at Your service, O Allah, I am at Your service.' He was never seen in any condition except remembering Allah, Glorified be He, and he was the most truthful of people in speech and the most eloquent in eloquence.

And indeed, it was said to Mu'awiya one day: 'If you ordered al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib to climb the pulpit and deliver a sermon, his deficiency would become clear to the people.' So he called him and said: 'Climb the pulpit and speak words that will exhort us.' So he stood, climbed the pulpit, praised Allah and commended Him, then said: 'O people! Whoever knows me already knows me, and whoever does not know me — I am al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, the son of the Mistress of Women, Fatima, daughter of the Messenger of Allah. I am the son of the best of Allah's creation. I am the son of the Messenger of Allah. I am the son of the possessor of virtues. I am the son of the possessor of miracles and signs. I am the son of the Commander of the Faithful. I am the one ejected from my right. My brother al-Husayn and I are the two Masters of the Youth of Paradise. I am the son of the Rukn and the Maqam. I am the son of Mecca and Mina. I am the son of al-Mash'ar and Arafat.'

So Mu'awiya said to him: 'O Aba Muhammad, describe the date fruit and leave this.' So he said: 'The wind inflates it, the heat ripens it, and the cold sweetens it.' Then he returned to his speech and said: 'I am the Imam of the creation of Allah, and the son of Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah.' So Mu'awiya feared that he would speak thereafter with what would enchant the people, so he said: 'O Aba Muhammad, descend, for what has occurred is sufficient.' So he descended.

key_terms.أزهد: Most ascetic, most renouncing of worldly pleasures
key_terms.السليم: One bitten by a snake; metaphor for extreme agitation
key_terms.المدفوع عن حقي: The one ejected from my right — reference to political dispossession
key_terms.فرائص: The muscles between the ribs and shoulders that tremble from fear
key_terms.لبيك: Labbayk — 'I am at Your service', the Hajj response formula

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Hasan say when Mu'awiya asked him to speak on the pulpit?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain going back to Imam al-Sadiq from his forefathers, describes the extraordinary piety and devotion of Imam al-Hasan ibn Ali (AS). It portrays his weeping when remembering death, the grave, resurrection, and the Day of Judgment. It also recounts the famous incident where Mu'awiya, attempting to humiliate Imam al-Hasan on the pulpit, was instead awestruck as the Imam eloquently proclaimed his noble lineage — son of the Prophet, Fatima, and Ali — and his rightful claim to leadership, forcing Mu'awiya to cut the speech short.
word_analysis: and the most ascetic of them
